blocker.location: 240/0, right exit chokepoint, on-screen stop position (44,12)
observations: 3 methodologically distinct approaches (raw Navigator.move! taps; Navigator.avoid_hostiles_and_push! default radius=16; avoid_hostiles_and_push! radius=32; avoid_hostiles_and_push! via a down-then-right alternate route) all converge on the EXACT same on-screen stop position (44,12) and the exact same HP floor (8/24 from a 24/24 start) -- technique-independent convergence, not a controller-skill gap.

2 OAM-confirmed tile=0x50 object pairs sit just past the chokepoint (screen x=70,y=30 and further east) -- static, non-mobile, 4-frame idle animation, never yet reached for a face+:a interaction test.

Room genuinely SCROLLS past this point (SCY shift observed, single tap moved y from 36 to 12) -- the chokepoint sits right around the scroll boundary, a plausible reason a fixed-radius avoidance primitive underperforms here specifically.
known_constraints: D12: no RAM writes to bypass the obstacle (0xDB5A must never be written)
no weapon/A-slot item confirmed owned yet
owner explicitly declined a D12 HP-write exception for this specific blocker and asked for a genuinely different approach instead

hypotheses.statement: The chokepoint is passable without any HP-floor regression below the already-established 8/24 by reading hostile OAM positions live each step and only advancing right when no hostile is within contact range (an opportunistic gap-dash), because the hostiles wander/patrol (documented elsewhere in this project) rather than permanently occupying the chokepoint -- a fixed-radius avoidance primitive (tested at radius 16 and 32) cannot exploit a moving gap the way a live polling loop can.
evidence:
Checkpoint lib_e240_confirmed.dump (24/24 HP, x=20 y=36, room 240/0, shield equipped).
2 sub-runs of a genuinely different, timing/patience-based technique: each iteration takes a
live OAM census via Navigator.nearby_hazards (correct HAZARD_TILE_IDS union, includes 0x6c per
this room's own MP11 lesson), and only moves right when NO hazard sits within a safe margin
(24px, distinct from both previously-tested avoid_hostiles_and_push! radii of 16/32) -- else it
idles in place (shield held, zero movement keys) and re-polls, letting the wandering hostiles
move before re-checking. No direction-biasing (unlike avoid_hostiles_and_push!): purely wait-or-
advance-straight.

Run 1 (coarse: one hazard check gates a full Navigator.move_holding! burst, up to 8 internal taps
/ ~240 frames per decision): 4 dash bursts + 6 waits, cost ~1080 frames. Converged on the exact
same (44,12)/8-HP-floor signature already seen 3 times (raw taps, avoid r16, avoid r32,
down-then-right). New finding from this run: at iteration 3 a WAIT (hazard already at 5.7px,
inside the 24px margin) still took 3 HP while Link was fully stationary -- the margin didn't
prevent contact, it just meant Link was standing still while hit. At iteration 7 the pre-burst
census read CLEAR (hazards.empty?) yet the subsequent multi-tap dash burst still cost 8 HP
(20->12) before landing at (44,12) -- a wandering hazard closed the gap mid-burst, invisible to a
once-per-burst check.

Run 2 (fine-grained: hazard census before EVERY SINGLE TAP, ~30-frame granularity, the most
charitable implementation of "read OAM live, dash only when clear" this project's primitives
allow -- steelmanning the hypothesis after run 1 showed the coarse version could be faulted for
under-polling): 27 single taps + waits, 3 committed steps (x: 20->28->36->44, matching TILE_SIZE
each), cost 1380 frames. Converged AGAIN on the identical (44,12)/8-HP-floor signature -- the 5th
independent technique to do so (raw taps, avoid r16, avoid r32, down-then-right,
now fine-grained OAM-poll-wait-dash). Sharper new finding: from tap 22 onward (once at x=44),
10 of the remaining 17 taps show ZERO position change (pos_before == pos_after exactly),
INCLUDING taps where the pre-tap OAM census read hazards.empty? (taps 22,23,24,26,37,38,41-44 --
right was pressed with a verified-clear gap and Link still did not move at all). This means
x=44,y=12 is not purely a hazard-timing problem: pressing right into a genuinely hazard-free
moment produced no displacement whatsoever, consistent with a real geometric/collision boundary
at this exact scroll position, not an avoidable moving gap. Additionally, HP still drained during
3 separate pure-idle waits at (44,12) (taps 30, 32, 45: -4 HP each) from hazards passing near that
fixed point even while Link took no action at all -- ambient chip damage independent of any
movement decision. HP hit the 8-floor at tap 45 (12->8), run aborted per the min_hp safeguard
before any further risk. 0xDB5A (LINK_HP_ADDRESS) was only ever read, never written.

Both runs, 2 independently-implemented granularities of the SAME core technique (live OAM poll,
wait for a verified-clear gap, then advance), converge on the identical stop coordinate and HP
floor already established by 4 prior fixed-radius/routing-technique attempts -- now 5 total
independent techniques landing on (44,12)/8-24 HP. The finer-grained run additionally shows
movement itself failing at (44,12) during confirmed hazard-free instants, and ambient damage
accruing while fully stationary -- both inconsistent with "a fixed-radius avoidance primitive
just isn't patient/precise enough to exploit a moving gap" (this hypothesis's core claim) and
more consistent with h_structural_gate_no_gap (x=44,y=12 reads as a real structural stop on this
screen, with hazard traffic passing through/near it regardless of Link's own timing).
GIFs: data/recordings/2026-09-19_240_0_gap_dash_test.gif (run 1, coarse),
data/recordings/2026-09-19_240_0_gap_dash_test_v2.gif (run 2, fine-grained).
Screenshots: room240_gap_dash_final.png, room240_gap_dash_v2_final.png (scratchpad).

READING: the blocking cell is not a byte-identical match to the ONE previously-sampled wall
signature (this room plausibly has more than one non-walkable tile type -- hedge vs water-strip vs
a wall-adjacent transition tile -- so an exact match was never guaranteed), but it IS a genuinely
distinct pattern from confirmed-open grass, has no OAM sprite explaining the block in this static
census, and reconfirms :blocked via a zero-risk probe. Combined with the prior session's own
strongest finding (taps 22-44 at x=44 showed zero displacement even during OAM-verified
hazard-free instants), the balance of evidence favors reading this as a genuine BG-tile/geometric
collision boundary at this exact column, not merely a hazard standing in the way at the moment of
each attempt -- supports h_structural_gate_no_gap's core claim over a pure hazard-crowding
explanation. Caveat, stated plainly: this is not a clean byte-for-byte wall-signature match, only
a single OAM snapshot (can't rule out a hazard occupying that exact cell at some OTHER instant),
and this is only 1 of the 2 independent supporting experiments this hypothesis needs before the
recovery flow would call it "supported" -- reported as "supports" for this one experiment, not as
proof.

hypotheses.statement: The 240/0 chokepoint damage is not purely from the wandering tile=0x6a/0x68 hostile: the 2 static tile=0x50 round objects near it (never contact-tested, closest approach only 25-30px) may be a variant of the oursin/sea-urchin hazard family already documented at riverside_flower_clearing (225/0, tile=0x5C/0x5E) -- a STATIC contact-damage hazard, not an active attacker. The signpost there explicitly says a shield protects against oursins specifically (dialogues.riverside_flower_clearing_sign, page 2: "Se proteger avec un bouclier!"), a claim never actually tested in-game (registry note: shield was only ever measured as partial knockback-mitigation against the WANDERING 0x60-family, never as a full block against a static oursin-type object). If true, deliberately walking into contact with a tile=0x50 object while shield-equipped (B held, facing it) should show ZERO HP cost on that specific contact, unlike contact with the wandering 0x6a/0x68 creature, which the D13 primitive already showed still costs HP even while shielded.

experiments.observation:
Checkpoint e240_confirmed (24/24 HP, x=20 y=36, room 240/0, shield equipped B-slot=4), 2 runs.
Run 1 (avoid_hostiles_and_move! bias toward :right): the hazard-avoidance dot-product picked
:up at step 3 (nearby 0x60-family wanderer), which -- per Navigator.move!'s own documented
boundary-rebase caveat -- silently crossed room_id 240/0->224/0 while still reporting :blocked;
9 further steps wandered in 224/0 (wrong room) burning HP 24->16 with the tile=0x50 object never
in OAM range. Discarded as a script artifact, not evidence either way.
Run 2 (plain Navigator.move_holding!(motherboard,:right,:b,min_hp:8) per step, room_id checked
every step to catch a repeat of run 1's silent room-exit): reproduced the established chokepoint
exactly -- stopped at (44,12), HP 24->8, still in 240/0, after 4 productive steps. OAM census
taken immediately BEFORE each damaging step cleanly attributes every HP loss to the wandering
hazard family, never to a tile=0x50 object: step2 (-1 HP, 24->23) nearest 0x60-wanderer at
28.2px (tile=0x50 present but at 43.9px, farther); step3 (-12 HP, 23->11) an under-tracked
tile=0x6c 'unknown hazard' sprite (Navigator::UNKNOWN_HAZARD_TILE_IDS, NOT in my wanderer query
until I checked it by hand) sat 5.7px from Link's pre-step position, no tile=0x50 object was even
on-screen at that moment (nearest_static: null); step4 (-3 HP, 11->8, the safety floor) a
tile=0x60 wanderer sat 2.8px away (essentially adjacent) while the nearest tile=0x50 object was
31.6px away -- matching, almost to the pixel, room_labels['240/0']'s already-recorded ~31px
closest-approach figure from the prior D13-primitive session. The static tile=0x50 object was
NEVER within Navigator::HAZARD_PROXIMITY_PX (16px) contact range in either run; closest live
reading was 31.6px, always with HP already at or crossing the 8-floor by the time the object
entered plausible range. Deliberate contact (walking INTO the object, facing it, shield held) was
therefore never attempted -- the HP floor was reached first, 3 productive right-pushes in, a 4th
technique-independent convergence on the exact same (44,12)/8-24 signature already seen 3 times
(raw taps, avoid_hostiles_and_push! r16, r32, down-then-right). Control comparison (not re-run,
from data/ram_registry.json's already-established Sept 16 2026 combat-contact test, 208/0): a
single stationary-approached 0x60-family wanderer took a full shield block (zero damage, 12-14
collision-seeking steps at 8.1px) in that room's less-dense setting; this run's denser,
multi-hazard 240/0 pocket (0x60 AND 0x6c both active near the chokepoint) showed only partial
mitigation -- real, non-zero damage on 3 of 4 productive steps despite the shield being held
continuously throughout (verified via Navigator.shield_equipped? and holding :b every internal
tap), consistent with this project's own established 'shield only partially mitigates in dense
multi-hazard scenarios, not a guaranteed full block' reading. GIFs:
data/recordings/2026-09-18_240_0_oursin_shield_test.gif (run 1, room-exit artifact),
data/recordings/2026-09-18_240_0_oursin_shield_test_v2.gif (run 2, the recorded attempt).
